{{Short description|Elliptic partial differential operator}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:''p''-Laplacian}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''''p''-Laplacian''', or the '''''p''-Laplace operator''', is a quasilinear [[elliptic operator|elliptic]] [[partial differential operator]] of 2nd order. It is a nonlinear generalization of the [[Laplace operator]], where <math>p</math> is allowed to range over <math>1 < p < \infty</math>. It is written as

:<math>\Delta_p u:=\mathrm{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2} \nabla u).</math>

Where the <math>|\nabla u|^{p-2}</math> is defined as

:<math>\quad |\nabla u|^{p-2} = \left[ \textstyle \left(\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_1}\right)^2 
+ \cdots + \left(\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_n}\right)^2 
\right]^\frac{p-2}{2} </math>

In the special case when <math>p=2</math>, this operator reduces to the usual [[Laplacian]].<ref name="E356">Evans, pp 356.</ref> In general solutions of equations involving the ''p''-Laplacian do not have second order derivatives in classical sense, thus solutions to these equations have to be understood as [[weak solution]]s. For example, we say that a function ''u'' belonging to the [[Sobolev space]] <math>W^{1,p}(\Omega)</math> is a weak solution of

:<math> \Delta_p u=0 \mbox{ in } \Omega</math>

if for every test function <math>\varphi\in C^\infty_0(\Omega)</math> we have

:<math> \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^{p-2} \nabla u\cdot \nabla\varphi\,dx=0</math>

where <math>\cdot</math> denotes the standard [[scalar product]].

== Energy formulation ==
The weak solution of the ''p''-Laplace equation with [[Dirichlet boundary conditions]]

:<math>\begin{cases}
-\Delta_p u = f& \mbox{ in }\Omega\\
u=g & \mbox{ on }\partial\Omega
\end{cases}
</math>

in an open bounded set <math>\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^N</math> is the minimizer of the [[energy functional]]

:<math>J(u) = \frac{1}{p}\,\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^p \,dx-\int_\Omega f\,u\,dx</math>

among all functions in the [[Sobolev space]] <math>W^{1,p}(\Omega)</math> satisfying the boundary conditions in the sense that <math>u-g\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)</math> (when <math>\Omega</math> has a smooth boundary, this is equivalent to require that functions coincide with the boundary datum in [[Trace operator|trace]] sense<ref name="E356"/>). In the particular case <math>f=1, g=0</math> and <math>\Omega</math> is a ball of radius 1, the weak solution of the problem above can be explicitly computed and is given by

:<math>u(x)=C\, \left(1-|x|^\frac{p}{p-1}\right)</math>

where <math>C</math> is a suitable constant depending on the dimension <math>N</math> and on <math>p</math> only. Observe that for <math>p>2</math> the solution is not twice [[Differentiable function|differentiable]] in classical sense.
